# Used EV prices down by over £7,000, but sales nearly triple 

- By Tom Seymour
- |
- 23 June 2025
- News

The average price of a used electric vehicle (EV) in the UK has dropped by £7,411 in just two years, falling from £30,441 in May 2023 to £23,029 in May 2025.

At the same time, the number of used EVs sold has surged by more than 180%, rising from 7,073 to 19,836 over the same period.

The latest figures from Marketcheck highlight a shift in the UK used EV market, with falling prices making EVs more accessible to a wider range of buyers.

The 24.35% price decline marks a record low, while the sharp growth in volume reflects rising availability and demand.

Monthly trends reveal a pattern of steady price reductions, interrupted by seasonal fluctuations in late 2023 and 2024.

December 2023 saw a brief spike in average prices to £29,710 before dropping again in early 2024. A similar uplift occurred at the end of 2024, followed by renewed declines.

January 2024 was a turning point, with a 49% jump in sales coinciding with a 10.7% drop in prices. In January 2025, volumes rose even more sharply, up 64.6%, as prices dipped again.

Alastair Campbell, head of strategy at Marketcheck UK said: “As the data shows, it is becoming increasingly more affordable to buy a used EV in the UK with prices reaching record lows in our latest monthly report.

"Marketcheck will continue to analyse emerging trends across the UK used car market."

###### Author: Tom Seymour 

###### Freelance writer

Tom Seymour is an experienced freelance journalist specialising in the automotive and business sectors, with more than 20 years’ experience reporting and analysing industry developments.

As a regular contributor to Bauer Media’s B2B titles Fleet News and Automotive Management (AM), he covers topics ranging from fleet operations and electrification to dealership performance, manufacturer strategy and the wider mobility landscape.

In addition to his writing, Tom presents and hosts webinars for AM, leading discussions with senior industry figures on key trends and challenges affecting the UK automotive retail sector.

He also plays a central role in shaping and delivering content for the annual Automotive Management Live show, developing sessions that explore innovation, leadership and operational excellence across the industry.

Since moving into freelance journalism in 2015, Tom has worked with a range of business, technology and transport publications from his “box in the garden” in Norwich.

Away from deadlines he is a former alternative rock drummer and committed movie buff, as well as a perpetually exhausted father of two lively goblins.
